title: Allegorical and Tropological Interpretations of Psalm 43
english: One falls into destruction. If someone, having left Zion, that is to say, virtue, rushes toward the evil called Babylon, turning back to the things behind, he receives a blessed thing; but those saying the things set forth, since they have become among the enemies, having turned back to the things behind, fell into filth (Ps 43:12).

Those saying these things are like certain sons who, similarly to a sheep being led to slaughter, are given to be food for those approaching them for their own benefit with words and life; but even among the Gentiles they were scattered by God, sowing the seed like farming, so as to change the Gentiles into the same quality as themselves. For one must not pay attention to those saying that God's portion was scattered among the Gentiles in the manner of captivity.

Not for honor, he says, having taken the people, he sent them away, but because of their sins they have been made submissive to enemies (Ps 43:13a); for through their sins they were given over according to the prophet.

Since we have fallen away from the aforementioned things through a life fearing destruction, we face our own disgrace (Ps 43:16), the shame of our face covering us so that we no longer have boldness, with the face of the soul uncovered to reflect the glory of the Lord.

From the voice of the one reviling and acting unjustly and speaking wrongly, he sees that the day of ruin is before him (Ps 43:17). And from the one displaying his terrible face, driving out an enemy, the shame of it covered his face.

The voice, having taken up perfect courage (Ps 43:18): for having heard many and various afflictions upon them and being coerced into forgetting God, they say, as it were, 'In the affliction of the Lord I remembered' (Ps 43:19b). God turns away some of the troubles from...

He abandons his own way, handing himself over to the desires of his own heart and to an unproven mind (Ps 43:20a). The earth and the underworld are a place of affliction; thus those having experienced the body of death are humbled (Ps 43:22b). The impressions in the heart must be addressed and examined (Ps 43:26).

If one speaks these things tropically, what is meant is this: since we are currently surrounded by the composite of pleasure and other passions, because of this, 'Our soul was humbled to the earth, having become low-minded, and also our belly was stuck to the earth, feeding on nothing heavenly but eating all things according to the nature of earth all the days of their lives.' But if the present text is explained allegorically, the soul stepping into the body says, 'Our soul was humbled to the earth.' Having fallen away from itself and from the blessed life of the heavenly, while thinking of the lower things, it says, 'Our belly was stuck to the earth,' for it feeds on nothing other than earthly things (Ps 43:27).

These say that they are worthy to receive help and deliverance, not by the grace of another but by His name. And these things are also said regarding the Savior, being worn down in the heart of the earth according to the season of passion, so that having risen, He might provide help and giving deliverance, giving His soul as a ransom for many. And He does these things for the glory of His name.

A goal for those making progress and changing from quality to quality is that the one at the summit of qualities should hasten (Ps 44:1), by which the corruptible and the immortal might be proven. Concerning this, the end being attained. Concerning those who shall be transformed, that is, those who are changed and have become eager from evil, sons of Kore turning all things into a song concerning the beloved, bringing forth and shouting. And the beloved here is the only-begotten Son of God. Concerning this, the triumphal song is sung, through whom He transformed, having given incorruption instead of corruption.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
